newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish Horseracing Authority to transform the Tote.
newsitem.headline: Irish Horseracing Authority to transform the Tote.

text.p: The Irish Horseracing Authority (IHA) on Wednesday said it would radically transform the Tote, a cash and credit betting service on-course and an off-course credit betting service, in Ireland.

The IHA said in its strategic plan for the development of the Irish Thoroughbred Racing Industry 1997-2001 that it planned to transform the Tote so that it contributed substantially to the income of the Authority for reinvestment and reduce the overall cost-base in Irish racing.
"The Tote has the potential to bridge the gap between the finance currently available to the industry, which is adequate, and the level of finance that it so desperately needs," the IHA said.
"We have set ourselves an ambitious target in relation to the Tote but we believe that it is realistic and attainable," it added.
It said in the meantime, and pending the generation of additional income from within, it would be looking to the Irish government for increased support.
The IHA said it was targeting an overall increase of 28 percent in on-course cash turnover during the period of its strategic plan to bring Tote cash turnover to 20.3 million Irish pounds.

It said it was forecasting that the Tote will establish a High Street betting business with turnover of seven million Irish pounds by the year 2001 while it was forecasting a further growth in Tote credit betting from 3.6 million punts to seven million punts.
This will bring the total Tote turnover from its 1996 level of 19.5 million punts to 34.3 million punts in the year 2001, the IHA said.
It said this revenue growth was dependent on a strong marketing drive and it had included an extra 0.5 million punts for this purpose between the years 1998 and 2000.

The IHA said if the right steps were taken to reduce significantly the cost of operating the Tote, with a turnover of 34.3 million punts by the year 2001, an overall net contribution of 2.5 million Irish pounds would accrue to racing.

"The capital cost of bringing this about will be substantial both in terms of restructuring (staff-related costs) and investment in technology and equipment. After the pay-back period, racing will have available a substantial new source of income to improve prize-money and develop the industry more fully," the IHA said.
The IHA said total Tote turnover in 1996 was estimated at 19.5 million Irish pounds of which 3.6 million punts is attributable to credit betting.

With Tote retention averaging 21 percent, the gross retention from the Tote in 1996 was estimated at 4.2 million punt but operating costs of 3.6 million punts were to be incurred in running the business with the result that the net contribution to racing from the operation of the Tote is estimated at 0.6 million Irish pounds.
